title: Multitenant Health Scorecard: Spec and Dashboard Template
author: Ariana Patel
content:
Overview

This document defines the Multitenant Health Scorecard: a compact, operator-friendly composite SLI design and a corresponding dashboard template intended to provide a single-pane health view for inference services that host multiple tenants. The scorecard synthesizes latency, correctness regressions, model-fallbacks, cache efficiency, and cost signals into an interpretable 0–100 health index and recommended remediation actions.

Goals

- Provide a robust, tenant-aware health indicator for platform operators and SREs.
- Surface actionable causes (latency vs. quality vs. cost) rather than just symptoms.
- Enable consistent routing of alerts and operator runbooks based on degradation type.
- Support phased rollout and telemetry-driven validation.

Intended audience

- Platform operators and oncall SREs
- Product and ML engineers responsible for model quality and rollouts
- Observability and telemetry owners

Health Score architecture

The scorecard computes a weighted composite of sub-scores: Performance (P), Quality (Q), Availability (A), Efficiency (E). Composite score S is an aggregate on a 0–100 scale:

- Sub-scores are normalized to 0–100 (higher = better).
- Composite score S = 0.40 * P + 0.30 * Q + 0.20 * A + 0.10 * E

Rationale for weights: prioritize latency/throughput (P) for user-facing systems, surface quality (Q) second to avoid silent regressions, keep availability (A) and cost/efficiency (E) visible but lower-weighted so cost spikes don’t mask severe latency/quality issues.

Sub-score definitions and formulas

1) Performance (P) — token-latency and tail exposure
- Metrics: p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, request_rate_rps
- Normalize: baseline targets (example): p50_target=60ms, p95_target=200ms, p99_target=400ms. For each percentile compute normalized component: C = max(0, 1 - (observed - target) / target) capped to [0,1].
- P = 100 * (0.5 * C_p50 + 0.35 * C_p95 + 0.15 * C_p99)
- Example: if p95 is 300ms with target 200ms then C_p95 = max(0, 1 - (300-200)/200) = 0.5.

2) Quality (Q) — correctness and regression signals
- Metrics: eval_prompt_set_failure_rate, llm-monotonic-score-drop, rerank-inversion-rate, customer-reported-quality-incidents (per 100k requests)
- Normalize: Q = 100 * max(0, 1 - weighted_failure_rate), where weighted_failure_rate = 0.6 * eval_fail + 0.3 * rerank_inversion + 0.1 * customer_incident_rate_normalized
- Notes: owner teams should map golden prompt sets to tenants to ensure representative coverage.

3) Availability (A) — model variant availability and fallback count
- Metrics: model_instance_unavailable_pct, fallback_to_compatible_model_rate, error_rate_5xx
- A = 100 * (1 - clamp(model_unavailable_pct*0.7 + fallback_rate*0.2 + error_rate*0.1, 0, 1))
- Rationale: penalize unavailable primary model variants strongly, because silent fallback hides real availability impacts.

4) Efficiency (E) — KV cache hit, batching utilization, cost per 1k tokens
- Metrics: kv_cache_hit_pct, batching_utilization_pct, cost_per_1k_tokens_usd
- Normalize: E = 100 * (0.5 * kv_cache_hit_pct + 0.3 * batching_utilization_pct + 0.2 * cost_efficiency_score)
- cost_efficiency_score = clamp(1 - (cost_per_1k_tokens_usd / cost_baseline), 0, 1). Baseline is per model-family and region.

Dashboard layout (recommended panels)

Top row: composite and sub-scores
- Tile: Composite Health (S) numeric + sparkline (1h/24h)
- 4 tiles: P / Q / A / E sub-score numeric + trend

Second row: causes and drilldowns
- Panel: Latency distribution (p50/p95/p99) by tenant (top-10 tenants)
- Panel: Golden-prompt failure rate by prompt set (bar chart)
- Panel: Model-variant fallback count (time series)

Third row: operator signals and cost
- Panel: KV cache hit heatmap by model shard
- Panel: Cost per 1k tokens (time series) with horizontal baseline annotations
- Panel: Active rollouts and canary divergence indicator

Queries (examples)

- P95 latency (PromQL):
  sum(rate(llm_request_latency_ms_bucket{job=\"runtime\", le=\"200\"}[5m])) / sum(rate(llm_request_count{job=\"runtime\"}[5m]))  # compute percentile via histogram_quantile in practice

- Golden prompt failure rate:
  sum(increase(llm_eval_prompt_failure_total[15m])) / sum(increase(llm_eval_prompt_total[15m]))

- KV cache hit %:
  100 * sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) / (sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) + sum(rate(kv_cache_misses_total[5m])))

Thresholding and color bands

Set clear color thresholds for Composite S and sub-scores:
- Green: >= 85
- Yellow: 70–85
- Red: < 70

Additionally, attach fast-path escalation triggers:
- Immediate P95 breach: p95 > 2x target sustained for 3 consecutive 1m buckets -> page oncall
- Quality regression alert: golden_prompt_failure_rate increase > 3x baseline in 15m window -> create priority incident and notify model owner
- Cost surge alert: cost_per_1k_tokens_usd > 3x baseline for 30m -> warn oncall and product billing owner (no page).

Alert routing matrix (example)

- P-dominant degradation (S falls because P < 65 and Q >= 80): page runtime-sre -> operator runbook: latency-profiling cookbook
- Q-dominant degradation (Q < 60): page model-quality -> model-owner and ml-reliability team
- Mixed severe (S < 50): page platform-ops + eng-leads, open incident bridge, run emergency-model-swap playbook.

Operator runbook (compact)

1) Triage (first 10min)
- Read composite and sub-scores. Note which sub-score(s) drove decline.
- Check active rollouts dashboard for overlapping deployments in last 30min.
- Execute fast synthetic probe: run golden-prompt set for top-3 affected tenants and compare traces.

2) Quick mitigations (10–30min)
- If P-dominant: pin traffic to warm model variant, reduce batch window, enable prefetched KV prefixes for affected tenant(s).
- If Q-dominant: roll back to previous model tag for the affected tenant or reduce temperature/sampling in generation config and engage ML owner.
- If A-dominant (fallback storms): throttle new allocations, scale-out pre-warmed instances in the region, re-assign tenant priorities.

3) Escalation (30–120min)
- Open incident ticket with initial RCA hypothesis, include synthetic probe results and top affected tenants.
- If the composite score remains < 50 after mitigations, invoke cross-team war room (platform-ops, runtime, ml-quality, product).

4) Post-incident tasks
- Add failing prompt examples to the model onboarding eval harness.
- Create or update dashboard panels to reduce blind spots identified during the incident.
- Run a degradation postmortem and add action items to the platform roadmap.

Rollout and validation plan

- Phase 1 (canary, 2 weeks): surface composite score for a single region and 15% of tenants. Compare score trends to existing SLOs and operator feedback.
- Phase 2 (expanded telemetry, 4 weeks): enable golden-prompt execution for top-50 tenants and add model-variant fallback counters.
- Phase 3 (global), add cost normalization per model-family, publish score to product dashboards and integrate with capacity planning.

Ownership and SLAs

- Dashboard owner: Observability team (primary), Platform runtime (secondary).
- Score definition owner: Platform SRE + ML Reliability (co-owners).
- Review cadence: quarterly review of weights and baselines, triggered review after any major runtime change or model-family onboarding.

Validation checklist before publishing to oncall

- Automated synthetic suite executes golden prompts and confirms baseline Q >= 90 for covered tenants.
- Composite S agrees with manual operator assessments in 90% of sampled incidents across a 2-week window.
- Runbook steps are tested in a gameday exercise.

Appendix: example JSON-serializable score snippet (for exporter)

- Exporter fields (flattened key/value pairs) to be emitted every 60s per model-shard/tenant pair:
  - tenant_id
  - model_family
  - composite_score (0-100)
  - subscore_p, subscore_q, subscore_a, subscore_e
  - p95_latency_ms, kv_cache_hit_pct, golden_prompt_fail_pct

Operational notes and tradeoffs

- Coverage: the scorecard depends on golden prompt coverage. For low-volume tenants where prompt sets are thin, treat Q as low-confidence and expose confidence bands in the dashboard.
- Noise: short-lived blips are smoothed with a 1–5 minute window. Provide side-by-side raw and smoothed charts for forensic work.
- Cost visibility: E is intentionally low-weight to avoid suppressing urgent performance/quality signals; product billing teams will use separate cost dashboards for chargeback.
